A_target.statement:
Let $p$ and $q$ be distinct [[Definition:Odd Prime|odd primes]].
Then:
:$\paren {\dfrac p q} \paren {\dfrac q p} = \paren {-1}^{\frac {p - 1} 2 \frac {q - 1} 2}$
where $\paren {\dfrac \cdot \cdot}$ is the [[Definition:Legendre Symbol|Legendre symbol]].

B_source.statement:
Let $\zeta$ be a primitive $p$th [[Definition:Root of Unity|root of unity]] and:
:$\displaystyle g = \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^{p - 1} \paren {\frac k p} \zeta^k$
be the [[Definition:Quadratic Gauss Sum|quadratic Gauss sum]].
Then:
:$g^2 = p^* = \paren {-1}^{\frac {p - 1} 2} p$

substitutions.the Legendre symbol (p/q): the action of raising the Gauss sum g to the q-th power mod q
substitutions.the prime q: the exponent/modulus in which g is manipulated
substitutions.roots of unity zeta: elements of a field extension of F_q

object_map.reformulation: Compute g^q modulo q in two ways - by the Gauss-sum square identity and by the Frobenius (q-th power) map - and equate.

validity_conditions: Work in a ring containing p-th roots of unity over F_q; the Gauss sum g satisfies g^2 = p* = (-1)^{(p-1)/2} p.
Frobenius gives g^q = (q/p) g (raising roots of unity to the q-th power permutes the sum by the symbol), while g^2 = p* gives g^{q-1} = (p*)^{(q-1)/2} = (p*/q).
Equating the two expressions for g^q yields (q/p) = (p*/q), which unwinds to quadratic reciprocity.
proof_plan: Form $g$ in an extension of $\GF q$ containing a primitive $p$th root of unity $\zeta$.

Equating the two evaluations of $g^q$, and using $g \ne 0$:
:$\paren {\dfrac q p} = \paren {\dfrac {p^*} q} = \paren {\dfrac {-1} q}^{\frac {p - 1} 2} \paren {\dfrac p q} = \paren {-1}^{\frac {p - 1} 2 \frac {q - 1} 2} \paren {\dfrac p q}$
which is the [[Law of Quadratic Reciprocity]].
{{qed}}
